Turn 8 — Walker (verbatim): **Observations — West Shore, Turn 8**
- Rough square of foundation stones, ~4m per side. Local limestone, unmortared, weathered. No corners true — builder's eye or haste.
- Stones: 8 visible, 30-50cm each, seated in sand. No post holes, no post moulds, no charcoal flecks in immediate matrix.
- No walls, no roof, no hardware, no glass, no ceramic. No tool marks visible on exposed faces.
- Sand shelf continues, firm. Driftwood line resumes 10m west, sparse.
- Bearing back to south shore start (095° mag). Inland: low dune ridge, then scrub transition visible 40m on.

**Actions**
- Probe stone joints with knife tip — sand, shell grit, no mortar residue.
- Brush top surfaces for inscriptions, dates, initials. None.
- Check alignment — rough cardinal orientation (N-S/E-W within ~10°).
- Scan inland scrub line for structures, paths, clearings. None visible at this distance.
- Drink, note time.

**Working hypothesis (guess)**: Failed outpost, navigation marker base, or shelter frame never completed. Limestone suggests local quarrying or ballast. No trade goods = pre-contact or very low-investment historic.

**Next**: Continue west along shore to see if driftwood line yields more, or turn inland toward scrub line if directed.
